Assume small-deformation, linear-elastic, homogeneous, isotropic solid mechanics.
The shaft is a solid circular cross-section of uniform diameter d along its full length, subjected to pure torsion only; no transverse shear force, no bending, no axial load, no stress concentrations, no keyways or holes.
Material is aluminum alloy 6061-T6 with shear modulus G = 25939.8 MPa (equivalently N/mm²).
Shaft length is L = 1500 mm.
Applied torque is T = 1 000 000 N·mm, constant along the length.
The angle-of-twist limit is φ_allow = 0.75° measured over the full length L.
Convert the angle limit to radians before substituting: φ_allow = 0.75 × π / 180 rad.
Use the governing torsion relation φ = T·L / (J·G), where J is the polar second moment of area of the solid circle, J = π·d⁴/32.
Solve algebraically for the minimum diameter: d_min = [32·T·L / (π·G·φ_allow)]^(1/4).
All quantities must be expressed in the consistent unit set N–mm–MPa (i.e., MPa = N/mm²) so that d comes out in mm.
Report the final minimum required diameter d_min in mm, rounded up to the nearest practical value, and state the governing equations used.
State explicitly that the design is governed solely by the angle-of-twist criterion; a separate shear-stress check is not required by this specification.
